prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Houston. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Houston for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific office names near you — will you tell me your Houston neighborhood or ZIP code? If you want, I can also look them up for you and return phone numbers, addresses, and short notes on each.

While you decide, here’s a practical plan you can use right away (quick, concrete, and safe) — who to call and exactly why:

Which practices to call (by type) and why
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery (OMS) practices — They handle surgical implant placement, extractions, bone grafts and IV sedation/anesthesia. Call them if you expect complex surgery or want sedation.
- Periodontists — Specialists in the gums and supporting bone; they often place implants, especially when bone grafting/soft-tissue management is required.
- Prosthodontists — Specialists in tooth restorations and implant crowns/bridges; call them when you want the final restoration planned by an expert in aesthetics and function.
- Multi‑disciplinary implant centers — Some practices have OMS + prosthodontist + lab on site for coordinated, faster care and single-provider warranties.
- University dental clinics (UTHealth School of Dentistry) — Lower cost, care supervised by faculty; good option if budget matters and you’re comfortable with students delivering care.
Why call all of these: some offices do both surgery and restoration in-house (convenient), but coordinated care with a prosthodontist plus an experienced surgeon often gives the best cosmetic/functional outcome.

What to ask when you call (quick script)
- “Do you place dental implants? How many implants do you place per year?”
- “Who will do the surgery and who will do the crown/restoration? Are both done in-house?”
- “Do you use CBCT 3D imaging and guided-surgery planning?”
- “What implant brands do you use and do you provide a written warranty?”
- “Do you do the bone grafting/sinus lift if needed? How often is grafting required here?”
- “What anesthesia/sedation options are available?”
- “Can I see before/after photos and patient references or online reviews?”
- “Do you accept my insurance? What estimate/fee breakdown can you give for evaluation, surgery, and restoration?”
- “Do you do a free/low-cost consultation or second opinion?”

What to look for (red flags and green flags)
- Green: board-certified specialists, lots of focused implant cases, use of CBCT and digital planning, documented before/after cases, coordinated surgeon + prosthodontist approach, clear fee breakdown and warranty.
- Red: vague answers about who does which part, no 3D imaging, “can’t show before/after photos,” pressuring you to decide immediately, unclear fees.

Practical next steps
1. Tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and any preferences (budget, sedation, weekend hours, insurance). I’ll return a short list of 4–6 specific Houston practices with phone numbers and a one-line reason to call each.
2. Use the script above when you call, compare answers, and get written estimates. If you want, paste the answers here and I’ll help compare them and recommend the best option.
